# The Veil That Tears Across the Sky

## Scripture

"And when Jesus had cried out again in a loud voice, he gave up his spirit. At that moment the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, the rocks split and the tombs broke open." — Matthew 27:50-52

## Reflection

Every October, the Orionid meteor shower streaks across our night sky. These aren't wandering stars but debris from Halley's Comet—tiny fragments that ignite when they strike Earth's atmosphere at breathtaking speed. What was once part of a distant, icy wanderer becomes a brief blaze of glory above us.

The tearing of the temple curtain was like that. From top to bottom—not bottom to top, as if humanity had clawed its way through. God Himself ripped the veil, and the fragments of that dividing wall scattered like sparks across history. The Holy of Holies, once sealed behind fabric and fear, lay open.

Meteor showers remind us that Heaven's barriers don't hold when God decides to move. The same God who shook the earth at Calvary still parts the veil between seen and unseen. When we gaze upward this season, those fleeting streaks of light whisper what the torn curtain declared: *The way in is open. Come through.*

## Prayer

Father, thank You for tearing the veil that separated us from Your presence. Like meteors blazing through the darkness, let Your glory pierce every barrier we've built. Draw us boldly through the open way Jesus made. Amen.
